reasons.plausibility: Microalloying with refractory elements is a known strategy to stabilize precipitates and improve high-temperature strength, which is scientifically sound and aligns with established metallurgy principles.
reasons.testability: Measuring yield strength and creep rate in alloys with varying Hf content at elevated temperatures, along with microstructural analyses, clearly determines whether the hypothesis holds.
reasons.usefulness: Proposing minor Hf additions to enhance high-temperature properties in HEAs offers a concrete, potentially impactful approach for researchers, though it is a relatively standard path in alloy development.
